messages:
Mei Chen: Heads up — we've started seeing a wave of GPU soft-resets in us-c1, ~18% capacity drop for inference pool A since 02:10 UTC. Error rates in prod routes spiked ~3x. :rotating_light:
Jorge Rivera: seeing the same, alerted by the autoscaler. There's a pattern of Xid 13 followed by NVML soft-reset and then an ECC correctable flood in the logs. Sample from node gpu-node-37:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:2c:00): 13, PID=24321 0x00000000 0x00000000
[ 1234.568123] nvml: ECC error corrected, 256 entries
[ 1234.569000] nvml: GPU reset initiated
```
Priya Patel: Is this across multiple instance types or a single SKU? Might be firmware-related.
Sam: Mostly p4d-8x and a few t4s popping too. Not isolated to one SKU, but concentrated in us-c1 AZ-a.
Alex Kim: Ops tool shows spike in ECC counts starting ~02:05 UTC, and infra-bot flagged a driver reversion on one host last night. Could be a rollout side-effect.
Mei Chen: We're draining affected hosts now. Rolling drain policy: immediate cordon, drain non-critical jobs, live migrate priority inference lanes. Can infra team get replacement nodes in the spare pool?
infra-bot: spare-pool status: 4 cold GPUs available, 0 warm. Estimated warmup time for replacements: 22 minutes.
Jorge Rivera: 4 spares won't cover sustained loss if this spreads. Suggest we open a regional capacity burst to other regions (us-w2) and change routing policy to prefer lower-load regions for non-data-local requests.
Priya Patel: +1 to cross-region burst but watch costs — burst to us-w2 could double egress for some requests. We should narrow to cacheable / stateless routes only.
Sam: I can update routing policy now. Which models should be excluded?
Mei Chen: Exclude sensitive private models (customer_v1, client_fin) — keep public and low-context endpoints for spillover.
Alex Kim: Also recommend rolling back the driver reversion from last night on the few hosts that had it, and hold off on any infra-level firmware pushes until root cause identified.
Priya Patel: I'll escalate to vendor rep (cc @ops-bot) and open a hardware replacement ticket for nodes with repeated resets.
ops-bot: Created ticket HW-78912 with vendor: NVIDIA partner support. Assigned: Jorge Rivera. ETA for tech swap: 48-72h.
Jorge Rivera: For triage next steps: 1) continue draining symptomatic hosts 2) pin routing for stateless spillover to us-w2 3) vendor ticket + log bundle from affected kernels 4) snapshot driver/kernel for rollback testing 5) monitor ECC/Xid metrics for 2 hours for regression.
Mei Chen: Agreed. Also put a temporary autoscaler cap to avoid aggressive reschedules that could thrash the fleet. Setting cap to +10% from baseline.
Sam: Done — autoscaler cap set.
Priya Patel: FYI, costs estimate for 2h cross-region burst to us-w2 ~ $3.6k extra. If we go >6h, recommend finance signoff.
Alex Kim: Noted. I'll coordinate real-time updates in this thread. If we see persistent Xid 13 from the same PCI addresses, we'll isolate PCI bus and mark for immediate swap.
Mei Chen: Thanks — wills keep an eye. Ping me if new nodes show >5 resets in 30m. :thumbsup:
